title: rwb-integration customer products read: login, contract field names, ACE view owner, endpoint and route names, masking rows and flag switch not settled
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 29, 37 and 41; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1, T5.2, T6.2, API-P2-011 and Appendix T-B DL43; Ownership Map tables (masking_rule, feature_flag) and API (GET /cases/{caseId}/customer-products); legacy RWB-E2-003 sections 3, 12, 13 and 14; FSD P2 Integration v3 change note and A1.5; Template and Rules v1 §R3
section: §3 Preconditions, §11 Data, §12.1 REST provided, §12.2 REST consumed, §13 Solution plan, §14 Messages, §15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the unsettled points of the read. (1) Login: no source names the per-service login of rwb-integration under DP-02, and the legacy story runs as the shared recovery_svc identity. (2) Product, party and freshness contract field names: the sources name the legacy Java types PartyProductView, CasePartyView and DataProductFreshness and the LDM fields DF-ACE-280 to DF-ACE-285, not the JSON field names of the target contracts, and Architecture v5 slide 15 gives rwb-source-data /customers/{id} and /accounts/{id} only, so the product read path appears in no source. (3) Source conflict on the ACE view: Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29 and 37 and ADR-010 say that only rwb-source-data reads the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views, while TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 (view B11), T5.2 and API-P2-011 say P2 reads v_ace_party_product directly; by R-PREC the architecture wins and the TSD wording is superseded. (4) Endpoint field names: the response type CustomerProducts and its items are named, but the JSON field names and the problem body shape are fixed by no source. (5) Panel route: SCR-03's other products panel is served by the gateway-bff composite route under DP-19, and the route path, the screen-model field list and the merge order are not specified. (6) Masking row shape: masking_rule is owned by rwb-access in the Ownership Map, the legacy story marks the role split as assumed under DL26, and the row shape behind the policy is not specified. (7) Flag switch: feature flags belong to the platform library by the R-PREC default ruling (Ownership Map feature_flag is PLT), while TSD P2 v3 T3.1 defines feature_flag and feature_flag_change in rwb_integration, and the legacy flag name rwb.integration.customer-products has to be carried to that library. An eighth point sits in the same row: the FSD P2 Integration v3 change note rewrites MSG-P1-001, and the FSD outranks the story master under R-PREC, so the story uses the FSD wording.
evidence: TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 'P2 reads the views in T1.1 directly and calls nothing in P1 for inbound data' and T6.2 'The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views only' against Architecture v5 slide 9 'only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views' and slide 37 'Views read only by rwb-source-data'; TSD P2 v3 API-P2-011 'Read the other products of the case's borrowers from v_ace_party_product, joined on case_party.person_key, masked by role'; Ownership Map tables feature_flag 'Feature flags stay with the platform library (PLT, R-PREC default ruling); P2 serves the admin API against the library, despite TSD P2 v3 defining feature_flag and feature_flag_change'; legacy RWB-E2-003 section 3 '(assumed: unmasked for RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT, masked to the last four digits for every other role)'; TSD P2 v3 Appendix T-B DL43 blocks v_ace_party_product until RWB-ACE-001 lands.
area: Integration (P2) customer products read: contract, access and edge
proposed: Keep the endpoint with P2 on the base /api/recovery/integration/v1 (Ownership Map row, DP-13); read the holding and the DP02 freshness through the rwb-source-data contract, because Architecture v5 and ADR-010 outrank TSD P2 v3; read the parties and the linked accounts through the rwb-case contract; read the authorise check and the masking rule through the rwb-access contract; write the PII access event through ACE Common (INT-22); keep rwb.integration.customer-products as the flag name on the platform flag library; fix the contract field names in the P1, P3 and P4 contract stories and the response names in the rwb-integration baseline; fix the composite route in RWB-PLT-N001-CON; adopt the FSD P2 v3 wording of MSG-P1-001. Confirm with the ACE team that rwb_integration needs no grant on the recovery schema.

title: rwb-integration credit approval pack: login, contract field names, NLEADS read, the ownership split, the integration-base resource placement and the approval-level values are not settled by any one source
source: WP B-P2-02; legacy RWB-E2-006; Ownership Map v1; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 and A1.5; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 and T-A.1/T-A.2 (API-P2-012, API-P2-013 retired); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 16, 41 and 43; RWB-P3-E2006-APP
description: One combined gap covers everything this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login. (2) The exact JSON field names of the contracts this slice consumes are given nowhere: the rwb-source-data account, collateral, freshness and NLEADS credit-decision reads; the rwb-treatment plan-terms read and credit-result record; the rwb-document checklist read; the rwb-case read, action and reference-data read; and the rwb-access delegation and authorise answers. (3) The NLEADS credit-decision operation and its field shape do not exist in any source: TSD P2 v3 API-P2-012 reads v_ace_credit_decision in P2, while DP-05 and Architecture v5 slide 41 make rwb-source-data the only reader of the ACE views, and the tier 2 view waits on DL43. (4) The ownership split is a split of one legacy story across four owners and is fixed only by the plan and the Ownership Map: the case-side pack, the route state, the queue and the case-side record are rwb-case's (RWB-P3-E2006-APP); the four treatment columns nleads_ref, credit_result, credit_result_reason and credit_result_at and the treatment state are rwb-treatment's (S2 story of this key); the delegation of authority is rwb-access's (P4) and the approval routing P7's; the two integration-base resources stay with rwb-integration. The split makes the same pack composed twice, case-side and integration-side, and makes one decision produce a record at each owner, neither of which any source settles. (5) The placement of the two resources conflicts across sources: the Ownership Map keeps both with P2 (the GET on API Specification v4, the POST on v2 and absent from v3 and v4), TSD P2 v3 retires the result operation as API-P2-013 and removes the four treatment columns, FSD P2 v3 is outbound-file only and puts NLEADS out of scope, and the Architecture v5 service contract slide lists only GET /interface-runs, POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, FileDelivered and FileFailed for P2. (6) The new request and response shapes on the integration base are taken from the legacy CreditPack and CreditResult shapes because no contract fixes the JSON form, the error body or the header set beyond If-Match and Idempotency-Key. (7) The input age limit of 1 business day for balances is a legacy assumption (DL22) and is read as a reference row. (8) The approval-level values in the legacy criteria are inconsistent: AC2 records level L5 for a plan the Background puts at L6 or higher, and AC7 refuses level L6 for a plan that needs L5; both are copied unchanged, the comparison rule (at or above the level rwb-access returns) is applied, and the values are left to the delegation owner.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 3 (input age limit 1 business day, assumed, DL22), Background (plan needs L6 or higher), AC2 (approval level L5), AC7 (L6 refused for a plan that needs L5), section 12 (CreditPack and CreditResult shapes, CaseEvents.raise, DelegationQuery, TreatmentCommands, CaseDocuments) and section 13 (feature flag rwb.integration.nleads-pack, four new treatment columns); Ownership Map v1: GET /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-pack owner P2, POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-result owner P2 on API Specification v2 and absent from v3 and v4, delegation_limit owner P4, treatment owner S2, reference_row and recovery_case owner P3; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 (in scope: outbound adapters only) and A1.1 out of scope (NLEADS lands in ACE and is read through the views); TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 (v_ace_credit_decision, tier 2, read by API-P2-012), T-A.1 API-P2-012 (credit-pack) and API-P2-013 (retired, four treatment columns removed); Architecture v5 slide 16 rwb-integration IN REST GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, OUT FileDelivered and FileFailed, slide 41 (rwb_integration owns interface config, file runs, outbound items, ACE integration paths), slide 43 (FileDelivered, FileFailed on rwb.integration.events.v1) and slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s); no source names the rwb-integration login, the contract field names, the reference-data read path or the SCR-14 composite route
proposed: Settle in the wave 2 contract review: the rwb-integration login with the ACE DB owner; the two resources' placement in the Service Contract Catalog, with the P2 catalogue line and the retirement entry of the technical specification reconciled; the operation names and field sets of the rwb-source-data NLEADS read, the rwb-treatment result record, the rwb-case read, action and reference-data read, and the rwb-access delegation answer; one owner for the pack composition on SCR-14 and one record owner per decision; the reference-data read path; and the AC2 and AC7 approval levels against doa.txt item 2.1.1. Record the outcome in the contract stories and the gap and assumption registers; no business value changes in this story.

title: The rwb-integration login, the entry and fact JSON field names, the admin bodies, the mapping detail, the retry intervals and the ownership split of the ledger intake are not fixed in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14 to 20, 41, 42, 43 and 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11 and 13); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rulings on interaction, efs_ledger_outcome, processed_event, outbox_delivery, idempotency_key and the interaction operations); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 034 Interaction ledger on the case and from every channel v1.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P2 Integration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: Six values the app story needs are missing from every source. First, the login: DP-02 gives one login per service but no source names the rwb-integration login, its grants or its secret reference. Second, the JSON field names: the legacy story names the Java interfaces (InteractionLedgerWriter.append with LedgerEntryCommand, EfsContactHistory.outcomesFor, ContactQuery.byKey, CaseQuery.byId, CaseQuery.openCaseIdsForAccount, NoticeQuery.byId, InstructionQuery.byId) and the FSD and TSD name the tables, but no source gives the JSON field names, types, lengths or required flags of the append command, of the P1 EFS outcome read, of the P1 contact read, or of the rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-partner, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment fact answers. Third, the admin operations: TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 names API-P2-003 and API-P2-004 under the monolith base, and the Ownership Map keeps them in P2, but no source gives the request query parameters, the page envelope, the response bodies or the error bodies of the two operations on the /api/recovery/integration/v1 base, and no source fixes the shape of the RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task beyond its name and the role RW-PLATADM that receives it. Fourth, the mapping: BR1 of the legacy story gives the event-to-code mapping (InstructionIssued to HANDOVER, PartnerResultSubmitted to PARTNER_RESULT, NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered to LETTER, TreatmentApproved to OFFER, ProceedsMatched to PAYMENT, an EFS row to CONTACT) and those codes are kept unchanged, but no source states which payload element supplies the occurred time, the delivery status, the external reference, the from and to holder references or the source system of each entry, nor which of them an OFFER or a PAYMENT entry carries. Fifth, the intervals: no source fixes the retry intervals of the six ledger deliveries; the legacy story of this module uses retry windows of 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour, the FSD P2 v3 fixes 5 and 15 minutes for the WIN outbound file only, and the attempt limit of three appears in the legacy story and in the TSD but not as a rule of this consumer. Sixth, the split: the legacy story keeps the ledger, the EFS read step, the timeline and the masking in module P2, while the R-PREC default ruling and the Ownership Map move the ledger and the EFS intake rule to rwb-source-data (P1), the timeline to rwb-case (P3), the masking to rwb-access (P4) and the portal to rwb-partner (S9), and TSD P3 v3 defines the interaction table in P3 and TSD P2 v3 defines efs_ledger_outcome in P2; the intake slice that is left in P2 is therefore a reading of the default ruling over those documents and not a statement of one of them.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 12 names the Java interfaces and the tables but no wire shape; section 13 adds six columns to interaction and keeps the append-only trigger and efs_ledger_outcome; AC8 fixes three retries and the task for RW-PLATADM but no interval; BR1 gives the codes only. FSD P2 v3 A2.7 AC-EXC-P2-007-03 and AC-EXC-P2-007-07 give the dedupe key shapes EV-10:TRT-0001:v1 and EV-26:ALS:2026-11-10 and the hit count rule. TSD P2 v3 T3.2 gives LOV-OUTBOX-DELIVERY PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION and T4 gives the last-failure task; T-A.1 gives API-P2-003 and API-P2-004 with their rights and no body. Arch v5 slide 41 gives the schema rwb_integration, the first path /interface-runs and the queue rwb-integration but no login; slides 42 and 43 give the seven producer topics and the consumers; slide 44 gives JOB-02 and JOB-04 as event-started. The ownership rulings on interaction, efs_ledger_outcome, processed_event, outbox_delivery, idempotency_key, GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions and POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions carry the conflicting x-module and the default ruling.
proposed: Approve the five assumptions of RWB-P2-E2034-APP in the contract review of RWB-P2-E2034-CON before the app story starts: the login from the ACE DB story, the element names of the append command and of the five fact answers, the bodies of the two admin operations and the RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task, the per-type mapping of the occurred time, the delivery status, the external reference and the holder references, the retry intervals of 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour with the limit of three attempts, and the reading of the default ruling that leaves the ledger in P1, the timeline in P3, the masking in P4 and the portal in S9.

title: The append, EFS and contact wire shapes, the admin operation bodies, the dedupe key of each type and the ordering of the append and the inbox are not stated for the intake contract
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rulings on interaction, efs_ledger_outcome, processed_event, outbox_delivery and the two interaction operations); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 20, 41, 42, 43 and 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slide 11); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P2 Integration v3.md (A2.7); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md (T3.1, T3.2, T4 and T-A)
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC4 and AC5; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.3; 12.7; 12.8
description: A contract cannot be faked where the source is silent, and six elements of this contract are silent. First, the P1 append: the legacy story calls InteractionLedgerWriter.append inside the delivery transaction, and the R-PREC default ruling moves the writer to rwb-source-data, so the append is now one REST hop; no source states the wire command, the answer, the repeated-key answer or the error classes, and no source states the order in which the append and the inbox row are written, which is the only way the legacy once-only guarantee survives a service boundary. Second, the EFS and contact reads: the Ownership Map names no path for either, so the operation names, query parameters and field names are unknown. Third, the fact contracts: the Ownership Map names paths for the case read, the notice read and the treatment read but not for the single-instruction read, the proceeds read or the case-list account filter, and no source gives the element names of any of the five answers. Fourth, the admin operations: TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 fixes the method, the path suffix, the right and the Idempotency-Key header of API-P2-003 and API-P2-004 but not the query parameters, the page envelope, the response body or the error body, and no source gives the shape of the RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task. Fifth, the dedupe key: the FSD gives two example shapes only, EV-10:TRT-0001:v1 and EV-26:ALS:2026-11-10, and no source states the business key of the partner result, of the notice pair or of the treatment, so the key of each of the seven types is derived and not stated. Sixth, the state rule: the TSD lists the four delivery states and the last-failure task but not the legal moves between them, the resend rule for a delivery that is not in EXCEPTION, or the upgrade path of a field name that removes nothing.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 12 states that the writer must run in the caller transaction and section 13 stores the entry inside the same module; the ownership ruling on interaction records that the ledger stays with P1 despite TSD P3 v3 defining the table. FSD P2 v3 AC-EXC-P2-007-03 and AC-EXC-P2-007-07 give the two key examples and the hit count rule. TSD P2 v3 T3.2 gives LOV-OUTBOX-DELIVERY, T4 gives the one-delivery-per-consumer rule and the RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task name, and T-A.2 gives API-P2-003 and API-P2-004 without a body. Arch v5 slide 11 gives the inbox dedupe and the transactional outbox, slide 20 gives the per-service schema with outbox and inbox, and slide 41 gives the schema and the base. No AsyncAPI document for the four owner topics and no OpenAPI document for the P1 append is in the source set.
proposed: Approve the two assumptions of RWB-P2-E2034-CON at the contract review before the baseline is tagged: the wire shapes of the append, the two P1 reads, the five fact answers and the two admin operations with the RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task, and the dedupe key, the state moves and the append-before-inbox order with the repeated-key answer treated as success.

title: The consumer group names, the offset policy, the retry scan interval, the lag and alert thresholds, the build ID format and the fixture owner of the intake deployment are not fixed in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 20, 24, 33, 41 and 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11 and 12); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rulings on processed_event, outbox_delivery and idempotency_key); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md (T4 and T-A)
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.4; 12.5; 12.6; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The deployment needs nine values that no source fixes. The consumer group names of the intake and of the EFS read step, and whether they are one group across four topics or one group per topic, are not stated; only the logical consumer name ledger-channels survives from the legacy story and the platform rule names topics and topics only. The offset reset policy, the maximum poll, the commit point relative to the inbox row, the partition count and the rebalance behaviour are not stated. The retry scan interval is not stated: the platform relay runs every minute by the job map, but the scan that wakes an outbox_delivery after its next attempt has no stated interval, and the retry intervals of 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour of the legacy module are not confirmed for this consumer. The lag threshold of each of the five consumed topics, the alert threshold of the exception queue count, the alert threshold of the append failure rate and the stuck-run threshold of the EFS read step are not stated; the platform alert catalogue carries message identifiers, not values, and no source names an identifier or a text for a lag alert or for an EFS trigger alert in this service. The build ID format and the worker versioning policy are named as platform capabilities but not specified. The owner of the synthetic fixtures of the smoke run, and whether a synthetic delivery may be parked in a shared environment, is not stated. The replica counts, resource sizes, probe timings and the UAT promotion rule are environment values with no baseline.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 puts the outbox sender on a one-minute interval for every service and gives no other interval; slide 33 gives the morning run and the 16:00 window as the busy times but no threshold; slide 24 and the Temporal and Drools design slide 11 give the namespace, the task queue and worker versioning as capabilities; slide 41 gives the queue rwb-integration and the schema rwb_integration but no group, no offset rule and no login. TSD P2 v3 T4 gives the four delivery states and the last-failure task, and T-A gives the two admin operations, with no operational value. The ownership rulings on processed_event, outbox_delivery and idempotency_key record them as library objects created in every service schema and fix no deployment value.
proposed: Approve the two assumptions of RWB-P2-E2034-OPS in the release readiness review: the two consumer groups with their offset policy and commit point, the scan and retry intervals, the lag and alert thresholds, the build ID format and versioning policy, and the fixture ownership of the smoke run, all carried as environment values and never as code.

title: rwb-integration next action resolution: login, ownership of the read path, contract field names, operation names, Schedule values, message texts, legacy rule values and the timer vocabulary not settled
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 41, 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 12, 13 and 15; Ownership Map API row GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action (owner P3) and tables rule_row and rule_package_version (P7), reference_row and reference_version (P3), job_catalog (P2) and feature_flag (PLT); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1, T3.2, T5.2, API-P2-009 and Appendix T-B; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.2, A2.7 and the requirements served; legacy RWB-E2-035 sections 3, 4, 7, 12, 13 and 14; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R5.5, §R7.2 and §R9
section: §3 Preconditions, §5 Exception paths, §11 Data, §12.1 to §12.7, §13 Solution plan, §14 Validation and messages
description: One combined row for the unsettled points of this key. (1) Login: no source names the per-service login of rwb-integration under DP-02, and the legacy story runs under the shared recovery service identity. (2) Ownership conflict: the Ownership Map keeps GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action with P3 (API Specification v4 x-module P3; Arch v5 slide 41, P3 owns the case, the CMMN state, the queues, the tasks, the allocation and the timers), while this work package assigns the story to rwb-integration; the ruling taken is that rwb-integration serves the path under /api/recovery/integration/v1 (DP-13) and rwb-case keeps the case row, the four next action columns and the write, and the map row must be corrected to record it. (3) Contract field names: the sources name the legacy Java shapes NextAction, RuleRow, RoleInfo and RuleRef and the LDM fields DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053 and DF-REF-002 to DF-REF-011, not the JSON field names of the P3 case read, the P3 case list, the P3 next action write, the catalog operation of RWB-P3-E2042-CON, the P3 reference data and parameter reads or the P7 decision log read; the write path of the fill is named by no source at all, and the rwb-access authorise contract that the resolve, the read and the fill call, RWB-P4-E1037-CON, is not in the contract-dependency row of this key, so it is named in section 12.2 and carried here. (4) Operation names: the legacy interfaces NextActionAssigner.assign and NextActionCheckStep become POST /next-actions:resolve, GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action and the fill POST /cases/{caseId}/next-action, and no source fixes the colon path or the choice of POST for the fill. (5) Schedule: the legacy step is JOB-05 Timer check, every 5 minutes on Quartz, and the target is a Temporal Schedule named next-action-check on rwb-integration; neither the name nor the catch-up window, the overlap window and the backfill limit is fixed by a source, while Arch v5 slide 44 lists JOB-05 as retired durable timers with owner all and the Ownership Map ruling on the timer table retires JOB-05 and TimerDue. (6) Message texts: MSG-P2-023 is a new message of the legacy story and its text is the story master's, not the catalogue's, and the platform texts of MSG-GEN-004, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are reused here without a catalogue entry that names this key. (7) Rule values: package version RES-2026.12 and the rows R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07 with their action, owner role and timer are legacy values of the story master; they are kept unchanged and must match the registry rows that RWB-E2-042 and RWB-P7-E2035-APP load, and the legacy Background of RWB-E2-035 gives R-SET-13 the version RES-2026.12 while TC-E2-035-11 gives it SET-2026.12. (8) Timer vocabulary: the legacy calls the sweep JOB-05 and its step NextActionCheckStep, the timer table ruling retires JOB-05, and the name next-action-check is this work package's; the three vocabularies coexist in the legacy text of the criteria and are read as one mechanism.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-035 §12 names GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action and the interfaces NextActionAssigner.assign, TimerSpecResolver.dueDate, RuleCatalog.row, DecisionLogQuery.latestStateChange and ReferenceData.role; the Ownership Map row GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action reads owner P3 with no ruling text; the work package JSON for RWB-P2-E2035 places all three stories in rwb-integration; legacy §4 step 7 names JOB-05 every 5 minutes while Arch v5 slide 44 lists JOB-05 as retired durable timers owned by all; legacy §7 names the package version RES-2026.12 and the rules R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07; TSD P2 Integration v3 names no next action table and no next action endpoint, so the operation and table shapes have no technical source.
area: Contract, ownership, scheduling, messages, rule data
owner_role: Solution architect; contract owners of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision; platform workflow kit owner
proposed: Keep the story in rwb-integration as planned; serve GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action from the integration base under DP-13 and let rwb-case keep the case row and the write; fix the consumed field names in the rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision contract baselines; fix the three operation names, the next-action-check Schedule values and the five message texts in RWB-P2-E2035-CON; carry the legacy rule values unchanged into the registry; correct the Ownership Map row so that the P2 service owns the read and the P3 service owns the write; and record in the timer register that JOB-05 is retired and next-action-check replaces its next action step.

title: rwb-integration next action contract: the read path ownership, the three operation names, the consumed shapes, the Schedule values and the timer vocabulary are not fixed by a source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41 and 44; Ownership Map API row GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action (owner P3) and tables job_catalog (P2), decision_record (PLT), rule_row (P7) and reference_row (P3); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 and T3.2 (job_catalog, feature_flag) and Appendix T-B; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 12, 13 and 15; legacy RWB-E2-035 §12, §13 and §14; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R5.7 and §R9
section: §1 Story, §10 Authority, §11 Data, §12.1 to §12.7, §14 Validation and messages
description: One combined row for the contract baseline of this key. (1) Login: no source names the per-service login of rwb-integration under DP-02, and the contract names a workload identity it cannot resolve. (2) Ownership conflict: the Ownership Map keeps GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action with P3 while this work package places the story in rwb-integration; the contract reconciles them by serving the path from the integration base (DP-13) and leaving the case row and the write with rwb-case, and the map row stays uncorrected until the ruling is entered. (3) Contract field names: the consumed shapes of the P3 case read and write, the P3 case list, the catalog operation of RWB-P3-E2042-CON, the P3 reference data and parameter reads and the P7 decision log read are named by legacy Java types and LDM field IDs only; the JSON property names, the required flags, the query parameters and the write path of the fill are fixed by no source; and the rwb-access authorise contract the three operations call, RWB-P4-E1037-CON, is not in the contract-dependency row of this key, so it is carried here. (4) Operation names: the legacy in-process interfaces become POST /next-actions:resolve, GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action and POST /cases/{caseId}/next-action, and neither the colon path nor the POST of the fill has a source. (5) Schedule: the legacy JOB-05 every 5 minutes becomes the Temporal Schedule next-action-check on rwb-integration; the name, the catch-up window, the overlap window and the backfill limit are this work package's, while Arch v5 slide 44 lists JOB-05 as retired durable timers and the timer table ruling retires it. (6) Message texts: MSG-P2-023 is a new message of the legacy story whose text the catalogue does not hold, and MSG-GEN-004, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are platform texts reused here without a catalogue entry for this key. (7) Rule values: package version RES-2026.12 and the rows R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07 are legacy values, are kept unchanged in the contract examples and must match the registry rows of RWB-E2-042 and RWB-P7-E2035-APP. (8) Timer vocabulary: the contract names a Schedule where the legacy names a job, and the legacy criteria keep the JOB-05 wording; the two vocabularies are declared as one mechanism.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-035 §12 publishes the Java interfaces NextActionAssigner, TimerSpecResolver, RuleEvaluator, RuleCatalog and DecisionLogQuery with no HTTP path except the read; the Ownership Map row GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action reads owner P3 with no ruling; TSD P2 Integration v3 has no next action endpoint, no next action table and no job row for the sweep, so the contract fixes names the technical sources do not carry; Arch v5 slide 44 lists JOB-05 as every 5 min, owner all, retired durable timers.
owner_role: Solution architect; contract owners of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision; platform workflow kit owner
proposed: Baseline the contract with the three operation names, the nine consumed shapes, the split note, the workflow and Schedule contract and the error mapping; have the rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision contract owners confirm or correct the element names at the review; record the read path ruling in the Ownership Map; and confirm the five message texts in the catalogue.

title: rwb-integration queue-write adapter: the operation owner, the login, the consumed contract field names and the replay window are not fixed by one source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 036 Queue write interface for models and agents v1.md; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api POST /queues/{queueId}/placements; tables recovery_case, queue, assignment); Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 20 and 41
section: Legacy §3, §4, §10, §12 and §13; Ownership Map api and tables; TSD P2 v3 T3.1; Architecture v5 slides 14, 16, 20 and 41
description: The P2 story of legacy RWB-E2-036 builds an adapter whose operation, login, consumed contracts and replay window no single source fixes. (1) Ownership: the legacy story places POST /api/recovery/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements in the P2 module and its §13 puts the code in recovery/casewf/placement, while the Ownership Map keeps POST /queues/{queueId}/placements with P3 rwb-case, and the WP B-P2-02 assigns the story to rwb-integration. (2) Login: DP-02 gives one login per service and Arch v5 slide 41 gives the schema rwb_integration, but no source names the login literal. (3) Field names: the legacy §12 gives the PlacementRequest elements (caseId, reason, modelOrAgent, version) and the P3 contract gives caseId and reason only; no source gives the JSON element names of the rwb-case placement contract, of the rwb-case parameters contract that carries the approved callers list, or of the rwb-access authorise contract. (4) Status: the legacy AC1 expects 201, while RWB-P3-E1019-CON documents 202 for the P3 placement operation. (5) Replay: TSD P2 v3 T3.1 gives an idempotency_key table with a 24-hour retention and the columns id, idempotency_key, endpoint, request_hash and response, and the legacy §12 gives one placement per case and queue with 409 MSG-P2-024 on a repeat; no source fixes the replay window of the adapter or the column names of the decision_record library table beyond the standard record columns. (6) The admission decision code is D6 in the legacy AC3, which is also the code of the route decision D6 in the Drools design; the placement code is kept as the legacy has it. (7) Path: the caller-facing path on the integration base is named by no source; the legacy story serves the path on the monolith base and the naming rule replaces that base with /api/recovery/integration/v1, so the adapter serves the same suffix with no colon segment and no verb. (8) The message texts are the legacy texts and are copied unchanged.
evidence: Legacy §4 step 1 and §13 (P2 module, package recovery/casewf/placement, POST /api/recovery/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements); Ownership Map api POST /queues/{queueId}/placements owner P3 and tables recovery_case, queue and assignment owner P3; WP B-P2-02 story line RWB-P2-E2036-APP; Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-integration schema rwb_integration, rwb-case owns queues, tasks, allocation); TSD P2 v3 T3.1 idempotency_key kept 24 hours; legacy AC1 (201); RWB-P3-E1019-CON 12.1 (202 Placement); legacy §12 Idempotency row; legacy AC3 decision code D6
area: Integration contract ownership and field detail
proposed: Reconcile rather than duplicate: rwb-case keeps POST /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements and its behaviour, and rwb-integration serves the caller-facing admission and forwarding operation POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements on its own base, which forwards to the P3 operation with the four legacy fields plus the caller service identity and returns the P3 status and body unchanged; read the approved callers list through the rwb-case reference-data and parameter contract under the legacy key rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers; hold the stored answer in idempotency_key for 24 hours per endpoint and key with the TSD P2 v3 column set; write the admission decision record through the local decision-record library with decision code D6; take the login name from the rwb-integration DB story. The Ownership Map and the P3 contract are the authority for the P3 operation; this row records that the P2 story adds an operation on the integration base and does not take the P3 one.

title: rwb-integration queue-write adapter contract: the ownership of the placement path, the consumed contract shapes and the library table columns are not fixed by one source
source: RWB P2 E2036 APP Queue write interface for models and agents v1.md (this run); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api POST /queues/{queueId}/placements; tables idempotency_key, decision_record); Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 16, 20 and 41; RWB P3 E1019 CON Roles, teams and queues as data - contract v1.md
section: Contract sections 12.1, 12.2, 12.3 and 12.7; legacy §12; TSD P2 v3 T3.1; Architecture v5 slides 11, 14 and 20
description: The contract baseline of the rwb-integration adapter has to fix seven elements that no source fixes together. (1) Operation ownership: the Ownership Map keeps POST /queues/{queueId}/placements with P3 rwb-case and the WP B-P2-02 gives the same legacy key a P2 contract story, so the document must say which path is whose. (2) The JSON element names of the three consumed contracts (the rwb-case placement, the rwb-case parameters contract under rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers and the rwb-access authorise contract) are not stated by any source; the legacy gives PlacementRequest and RWB-P3-E1019-CON gives caseId and reason only. (3) The status of the P3 placement is 202 in RWB-P3-E1019-CON and 201 in the legacy AC1. (4) The row fields of the approved callers list (caller code, caller type MODEL or AGENT, service identity, approval state) are named nowhere; only the key is. (5) The column set of the decision_record library table beyond the standard record columns is not stated; Arch v5 slide 20 places the table in every service schema and DP-03 owns the library. (6) The replay window of the adapter is not stated for a placement; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 gives 24 hours for the stored response. (7) The rwb-integration login is not named by any source. The admission decision code is D6 in the legacy AC3, which is also the code of the route decision D6 in the Drools design; the placement admission keeps the legacy code. (8) Path: the caller-facing path on the integration base is not named by any source, and the legacy path carries the monolith base; the document serves the same suffix on /api/recovery/integration/v1, with no colon segment and no verb. The message texts are the legacy texts and are copied unchanged; the platform text of MSG-GEN-006 and of MSG-P4-001 is not restated.
evidence: Ownership Map api POST /queues/{queueId}/placements owner P3; WP B-P2-02 write list and story line RWB-P2-E2036-CON; RWB-P3-E1019-CON 12.1 (202 Placement) and 12.2 (POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise); legacy RWB-E2-036 §12 (PlacementRequest, 201) and AC1; Architecture v5 slide 11 (Idempotency-Key on every POST, stored response), slide 14 (rwb-access IN POST /authorise), slide 16 (rwb-integration schema and topic), slide 20 (own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record); TSD P2 v3 T3.1 idempotency_key and processed_event
proposed: Declare the placement on the integration base as the provided operation with the four legacy body fields, a required Idempotency-Key and the 201 shape of the legacy story, and declare the case-base placement as consumed and owned by P3; carry the consumed contracts as consumed with the placeholder for their JSON element names until their owners publish them; take the idempotency_key column set from TSD P2 v3 T3.1 and mark the remaining decision_record columns with the placeholder; state the 24-hour replay window as the platform rule; leave the login name to the rwb-integration DB story. Reconfirm the reconciliation with the Ownership Map at review: one owner per operation, two operations on two bases.
